 Ausar Thompson (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Thompson was initially probable for Wednesday’s game, so the status upgrade is unsurprising. The Pistons will stick with the five that started Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks, with Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, John Collins and Paul Reed rounding out the quintet. 
 Ausar Thompson 
 DET 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Ausar Thompson (ankle) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Thompson is back after sitting out Sunday’s win over the 76ers. He’ll take on the task of defending Jalen Brunson, while Daniss Jenkins returns to the bench. 
 Ausar Thompson 
 DET 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Ausar Thompson (ankle) is questionable to play against the Knicks on Tuesday. 
 Thompson missed Sunday’s game against the 76ers after injuring his ankle on Friday. Daniss Jenkins replaced him in the starting lineup, with Ron Holland II and Javonte Green taking on larger roles off the bench. The rotation would likely be similar if Ausar remains out, with Jenkins being the preferred streaming option. 
 Daniss Jenkins 
 DET 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Daniss Jenkins accumulated 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, one block and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the 76ers. 
 Jenkins started Sunday’s game for the injured Ausar Thompson and, as he did on multiple occasions last season, gave the Pistons solid minutes in that role. Jenkins’ final stat line lacked only a steal, as he was impactful on both ends of the floor. Detroit begins Week 2 with a Tuesday/Wednesday back-to-back, making it possible Jenkins gets another start in one of those games (if not both, if Thompson remains out).

 Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Duncan Robinson, John Collins and Paul Reed will start Sunday’s game against the 76ers. 
 Injuries have left the Pistons without two starters, as Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren have been ruled out. Jenkins and Reed will replace them in the lineup, with the latter offering greater long-term value since Duren will be out for at least two weeks.

 Ausar Thompson (ankle) is out for Sunday’s game against the 76ers. 
 Thompson will not play on Sunday after spraining his ankle during Friday’s win over the Heat. Ron Holland II and Javonte Green are two of the potential replacements in the starting lineup.

 Ausar Thompson (ankle) did not participate in Sunday’s pregame shootaround. 
 Thompson, who’s officially questionable for Sunday’s game against the 76ers, sprained his right ankle during Friday’s win over the Heat. If he can’t play, the Pistons have multiple options on the bench, including Ron Holland II and Javonte Green. Holland played 22 minutes on Friday, while Green played 13. 
 Ausar Thompson 
 DET 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Ausar Thompson (ankle) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the 76ers. 
 Thompson rolled his ankle, left the game and didn’t return in Friday’s win over the Heat. It’s encouraging that he’s listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the 76ers rather than being ruled out in advance. Still, it wouldn’t be a surprise if the Pistons exercise some caution and give Thompson more time off. In that case, Ron Holland II could see more playing time off the bench, though he’s not worth the risk to stream in fantasy leagues. 
 Ausar Thompson 
 DET 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters there’s no injury update on Ausar Thompson (ankle) and Jalen Duren (thigh). 
 Thompson appeared to roll his ankle while Duren grabbed his leg and headed to the locker room midway through the second quarter. While there was no update from Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff after the game, the team said Duren was questionable to return with a thigh injury. It’s unclear if either player will be available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers, though more information about Thompson and Duren’s status should be available Saturday. 
 Ausar Thompson 
 DET 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Ausar Thompson recorded a double-double on Tuesday with 11 points (4-of-8 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists and one steal against the Celtics. 
 Thompson made his presence felt on the defensive end, which contributed to Jayson Tatum only shooting 6-of-23 from the floor. That didn’t lead to many defensive stats, but those will come with time. However, Thompson was able to lead both teams in rebounding and was a solid secondary playmaker for them. It likely won’t last, but he did also make all three of his free throws after shooting 57.1 percent from the line last year. The most encouraging aspect of his stat line may have been that he played 33 minutes, which is way more than his 26.0 minutes per game last season.

 Jalen Brunson tallied 38 points (13-of-25 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), one rebound, seven assists, two steals and six three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls.
 Shooting 36.6 percent from the field in New York’s first four games, Brunson snapped out of that funk in a big way on Wednesday. Shooting 52 percent from the field and 6-of-10 from beyond the arc, the Knicks point guard finished with season highs in points, assists, steals and three-pointers. With the Knicks not arriving in Chicago until about 3 AM Wednesday, Brunson delivered an impressive showing. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Karl-Anthony Towns amassed 19 points (7-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 13 rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls.
 Towns had an injury scare in the first quarter after colliding with Bulls forward Noa Essengue and hitting his left hand/wrist on the court. After a quick trip to the locker room to get taped up, KAT returned to the game, with foul trouble limiting him to 28 minutes. We’ll see if Towns shows up on the injury report for Friday’s game against the 76ers.

 Amen Thompson had 23 points (10-of-16 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, three assists and one steal against the Bucks on Wednesday. 
 Thompson’s 23 points were his season-high after five games this year. After recording at least 10 rebounds in the first three games of the season, he’s grabbed just nine boards in his last two games. Thompson’s offense continues to improve, including his three-point shooting, which will only raise the floor of his fantasy value.

 Saddiq Bey finished Wednesday’s loss to the Nuggets with nine points (3-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three assists, two steals and one three-pointer.
 Bey, who played 26 minutes on Wednesday, replaced Jeremiah Fears (11/4/3/1 with one three-pointer) in the Pelicans’ lineup to begin the second half. After the game, Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley said he made the lineup change to get more size on the court. New Orleans outscored 28-22 in the third, with Fears scoring seven and Bey four. Given the circumstances, Bey’s role is unlikely to change anytime soon.

 Derik Queen tallied 11 points (3-of-6 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 12 rebounds, one assist and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Nuggets.
 Since playing 18 minutes in the season opener, Queen has logged at least 25 minutes in each of the last three as the Pelicans play without the injured Yves Missi. The second-year forward/center still has some defensive deficiencies to address, but he finished Wednesday’s defeat with his second double-double of the season. Even with Queen coming off the bench, Missi’s injury has raised his fantasy ceiling.

 VanVleet had his best game of the season as he scored 24 points and had four three-pointers. The 32-year-old point guard hadn’t scored more than 14 points in any of the other three games in which he played. VanVleet will look to keep it going Friday against the Mavericks.

 Jaden McDaniels with 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, and a three in 35 minutes against the Warriors. 
 There has been hope that McDaniels can grow his offensive game and he will have an opportunity to do so with Anthony Edwards out for at least two months. If he hit a couple more threes instead of going 1/8 from 3, this stat line would’ve looked even better than it already does. These next two months will be critical for Jaden’s development.

 Zion Williamson produced 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Nuggets.
 Williamson has scored at least 22 points in three of four games, with Wednesday’s total being a season-high. Also of note were the three steals, pushing Zion’s total to 11 through four games. Williamson may not be much of a defender, but he’s still managed to put up numbers in the steals column. If that continues, it could help offset the lack of three-point production.

 Christian Braun accounted for 15 points (6-of-13 FGs), four assists, three steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Braun’s 15 points matched his season high, and just as important for fantasy managers were the other categories. He didn’t grab any rebounds, but the assists and steals should benefit category-league managers. Braun’s coming off a disappointing 2025-26, and the Nuggets need him to bounce back if they’re to be a true contender in the West.

 Ayo Dosunmu had 17 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, four steals, and three 3-pointers in start for Anthony Edwards. 
 Ayo has shown that he can start and produce good numbers for when Anthony Edwards misses time. While he doesn’t have the best fantasy game, he can still be useful with some good scoring and some occasional outbursts with rebounds, assists, and steals. With Edwards missing two months, it wouldn’t be a bad idea to add Ayo in redraft leagues.
